title: Eikö … ole with singular owners
focus: Add the question ending -kö to ei: ei + -kö = eikö. Negative possession questions keep ole after the owner: Eikö sinulla ole palloa?
targetSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions

exercises.prompt: Choose “Doesn’t he have a car?” in Finnish. Use hänellä (“he as the owner”) and autoa (“a car”). Frame: “___ hänellä ole autoa”.
exercises.explanation: Ei + -kö gives eikö. Possession keeps eikö and ole unchanged for every owner; the noun uses its supplied partitive form.
requiredSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
exercises.targetSkill: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.Eikö hänellä ole autoa?: Ei + -kö gives eikö. Possession keeps eikö and ole unchanged for every owner; the noun uses its supplied partitive form.
optionFeedback.Eivätkö hänellä ole autoa?: Ei + -kö gives eikö. Possession keeps eikö and ole unchanged for every owner; the noun uses its supplied partitive form. This choice uses the wrong verb form.
optionFeedback.Eikö hänellä on autoa?: This choice changes the required polarity or leaves the required question pattern.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun

parts.formation: Ei + the question ending -kö = eikö. The front-vowel ending follows ei, independently of the noun.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: hän has the learned possession form hänellä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Negative possession keeps ole after eikö, with every owner.
auto + -a = autoa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
